guard_streams.write_limit: The January 2025 national snapshot and aggregate coverage figures are historical area-level evidence; they cannot establish current selected-parcel orderability, exact corrected r2 coverage or parcel-measured speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Spring 2025 Connected Nations update on 8 May 2025.
The update reports fixed broadband and mobile availability using a January 2025 snapshot.
The publication is an interim update to Connected Nations 2024.
Fixed broadband availability includes fixed-line and fixed wireless access networks.
The report covers service take-up on full-fibre networks and, for the first time, fixed wireless access networks.
It reports gigabit-capable availability for 25.9 million UK homes, or 86 percent.
It reports full-fibre availability for 22.5 million UK homes, or 74 percent.
The number of full-fibre broadband connections is reported as 9.0 million after an increase of 1.5 million.
The report estimates 48,000 premises could not access decent broadband from fixed-line or fixed wireless networks.
Ofcom states that the report data was used to update its broadband and mobile coverage checkers.

guard_streams.write_limit: Operator deployment plans are forward-looking and confidence-qualified; they cannot be written as current parcel coverage, live orderability or measured performance.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the 2025 planned-network-deployments report on 8 May 2025.
The report is based on communications-provider deployment plans as of January 2025.
The plans cover a forward period of up to three years.
The dataset includes privately funded operator plans and plans supported by public intervention.
The report excludes separate rollout aspirations of national and local public authorities.
The forward-looking report supplements the Spring 2025 snapshot of existing coverage.
If all plans were realised, full-fibre availability was projected to reach 28.8 million properties by January 2028.
The report states gigabit-capable coverage could reach 97 percent by the end of 2027.
Using only high-confidence plans, full-fibre coverage was projected at 86 percent by January 2028.
The report separately projects gigabit growth in rural and urban areas rather than treating all premises as a single current-status population.
